topic: Every positive finite strict neighborhood-shadowing separation occurs in a mixing nonsofic binary two-sided subshift with dense periodic points
title: Extending Meddaugh and Stephens' examples to every finite neighborhood-shadowing separation

creators.name: Zhang, Wenlin
creators.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

abstract: Extending the N=1 examples of Meddaugh and Stephens, Shadowing with small diameter sets of bounded cardinality (arXiv:2509.04312v1, September 4, 2025, Examples 3.4 and 3.6, Theorem 3.7), we answer their Questions 5.1 and 5.2 (Section 5, printed page 11) for every N>=1 by mixing binary subshifts with dense periodic points. For each m>=3, we construct a compact two-sided subshift with neighborhood (m-1)-shadowing but without neighborhood (m-2)-shadowing. A periodic phase cover supplies one fixed tracing set of at most m-1 points with arbitrarily small initial diameter. A progression with widely separated occupied sites forces the matching lower bound. Every member fails quasi-finite type and is nonsofic; in particular, m=3 gives another affirmative answer to Question 5.3. Moreover, the tracing points can all follow the pseudo-orbit at common periodic times, so even uniform syndetic tracing by each point does not characterize quasi-finite type.
summary: The progression subshift X_m has least neighborhood-shadowing bound m-1, is mixing, has dense periodic points, and is neither of quasi-finite type nor sofic, for every m>=3. Tracers have common periodic tracing times. Thus every positive finite separation occurs within mixing nonsofic binary two-sided subshifts, and uniform syndetic two-tracer shadowing does not characterize quasi-finite type.
